Nonrelativistic quantum mechanics

Words: 27
Quantum mechanics OurBigBook.com
Nonrelativistic quantum mechanics describes systems at speeds small compared with the speed of light, usually with time as an external parameter and evolution governed by the Schrodinger equation.

Berry phase

Words: 20
Quantum mechanics OurBigBook.com
A Berry phase is the geometric phase acquired by a quantum state transported around a closed path in parameter space.

Classical limit

Words: 22
Quantum mechanics OurBigBook.com
The classical limit is a regime in which quantum corrections or occupation-number discreteness become negligible and classical equations describe the relevant observables.

Parity (P)

Words: 99 Articles: 5
Quantum mechanics OurBigBook.com
Parity is the eigenvalue +1 or −1 of a state under spatial reflection.

Orbital parity ((−1)ℓ)

Words: 18
Parity OurBigBook.com
An orbital angular momentum eigenstate with quantum number ℓ changes by the factor (−1)ℓ under spatial reflection. Equivalently,
Yℓm​(−r)=(−1)ℓYℓm​(r).
(1)

Multiparticle parity (η1​η2​(−1)ℓ)

Words: 43 Articles: 1
Parity OurBigBook.com
The parity of a two-particle centre-of-mass state with intrinsic parities η1​,η2​ and relative orbital angular momentum ℓ is
η1​η2​(−1)ℓ.
(2)

Parity selection rule for a two-body decay

Words: 27
Multiparticle parity OurBigBook.com
If parity is conserved when a particle of intrinsic parity ηi​ decays into two particles of intrinsic parities η1​,η2​, then their relative partial wave obeys
ηi​=η1​η2​(−1)ℓ.
(3)

Spatial reflection (x↦−x)

Words: 26 Articles: 1
Parity OurBigBook.com
Spatial reflection reverses every spatial coordinate.

Pseudoscalar

Words: 20
Spatial reflection OurBigBook.com
A pseudoscalar is invariant under proper rotations but changes sign under a spatial reflection. In three dimensions the scalar triple product is a pseudoscalar.

Photon

Words: 13
Quantum mechanics OurBigBook.com
A photon is a quantum of the electromagnetic field with energy E=hν=ℏω.

Free particle

Words: 26
Quantum mechanics OurBigBook.com
A free particle has no potential energy, so its Hamiltonian is H=p2/(2m). On unbounded Euclidean space its energy spectrum has no normalizable lowest-energy eigenstate.

Ground state

Words: 104 Articles: 3
Quantum mechanics OurBigBook.com
A ground state is an energy eigenstate with the smallest possible energy. For noninteracting particles, the many-body ground state is obtained by filling one-particle levels subject to the particles' exchange statistics.

Ground-state energy

Words: 73 Articles: 2
Ground state OurBigBook.com
The ground-state energy is the smallest energy eigenvalue of a Hamiltonian operator.

Quantum variational principle

Words: 64 Articles: 1
Ground-state energy OurBigBook.com
For every normalized trial state ψ in the domain of a Hamiltonian operator H that is bounded below,
E0​≤⟨ψ,Hψ⟩,
(4)
where E0​ is the ground-state energy. Equality holds precisely when the trial state lies in the ground-state eigenspace.
Power-law quantum virial theorem (2⟨T⟩=n⟨V⟩)
Words: 30
Quantum variational principle OurBigBook.com
For a bound stationary state in a homogeneous potential V(λx)=λnV(x), scaling a normalized wavefunction gives stationarity of λ2⟨T⟩+λ−n⟨V⟩ at λ=1. Hence 2⟨T⟩=n⟨V⟩.

Energy eigenvalue

Words: 105 Articles: 6
Quantum mechanics OurBigBook.com
An energy eigenvalue E is an eigenvalue of the Hamiltonian: H∣ψ⟩=E∣ψ⟩ for some nonzero state ∣ψ⟩.

Energy eigenstate

Words: 21
Energy eigenvalue OurBigBook.com
An energy eigenstate is a nonzero quantum state represented by an eigenvector of the Hamiltonian operator. Its time evolution changes only its overall phase.

Energy eigenspace

Words: 8
Energy eigenvalue OurBigBook.com
The energy eigenspace for E is ker(H−EI).

Excited state

Words: 25 Articles: 1
Energy eigenvalue OurBigBook.com
An excited state is an energy eigenstate whose energy exceeds the ground state energy.

First excited state

Words: 13
Excited state OurBigBook.com
The first excited state has the smallest energy strictly above the ground-state energy.

Eigenstate

Words: 35 Articles: 1
Energy eigenvalue OurBigBook.com
An eigenstate of an observable is a quantum state represented by an eigenvector of that observable.

Momentum eigenstate

Words: 22
Eigenstate OurBigBook.com
A momentum eigenstate is an eigenstate of the momentum operator. In one dimension it is a plane wave eikx with momentum eigenvalue ℏk.

Quantum system

Words: 543 Articles: 24
Quantum mechanics OurBigBook.com
A quantum system is modeled by a complex Hilbert space; its quantum states describe preparations, while observables describe measurable quantities.

Quantum state

Words: 527 Articles: 23
Quantum system OurBigBook.com
A pure quantum state is a ray in a complex Hilbert space and may be represented by a normalized state vector.

Qubit

Words: 24 Articles: 1
Quantum state OurBigBook.com
A qubit is a two-dimensional quantum system. Its pure state is a ray in a two-dimensional complex Hilbert space and may be written α∣0⟩+β∣1⟩ with ∣α∣2+∣β∣2=1.
Qubit state
Qubit OurBigBook.com

Quantum number

Words: 16
Quantum state OurBigBook.com
A quantum number is a discrete label, usually an observable's eigenvalue, used to distinguish quantum states.

Quantum phase

Words: 47 Articles: 1
Quantum state OurBigBook.com
Multiplying a quantum state by one global complex phase does not change any measurement probability; relative phases between components can affect interference.
Global phase
Words: 25
Quantum phase OurBigBook.com
A global phase multiplies an entire quantum state by one complex number of modulus one. It does not change any measurement probability, unlike a relative phase between components.

Observable

Words: 391 Articles: 15
Quantum state OurBigBook.com
A quantum observable is represented by a self-adjoint operator; its possible measured values are spectral values of that operator.
Expectation value
Words: 15
Observable OurBigBook.com
In a normalized state ∣ψ⟩, the expectation of an observable A is ⟨ψ∣A∣ψ⟩.
Hamiltonian operator
Words: 357 Articles: 13
Observable OurBigBook.com
The Hamiltonian operator represents the total energy and generates time evolution through the Schrödinger equation.
Quantum symmetry of a Hamiltonian
Words: 53 Articles: 1
Hamiltonian operator OurBigBook.com
A unitary operator U is a symmetry of a time-independent Hamiltonian H when
U†HU=H,
(5)
equivalently [U,H]=0. A differentiable one-parameter symmetry U(s)=e−isQ/ℏ has a self-adjoint generator Q satisfying [Q,H]=0, so Q is conserved.
Conserved generator of a continuous quantum symmetry
Words: 17
Quantum symmetry of a Hamiltonian OurBigBook.com
If U(s)=e−isQ/ℏ and U(s)†HU(s)=H, differentiation at s=0 gives
[Q,H]=0.
(6)
In the Heisenberg picture,
dtdQ​=ℏi​[H,Q]=0.
(7)
Unitary time evolution
Words: 289 Articles: 10
Hamiltonian operator OurBigBook.com
A time-independent Hamiltonian evolves a state by the unitary operator U(t)=e−iHt/ℏ.
Time-evolution operator (U(t))
Words: 23
Unitary time evolution OurBigBook.com
The time-evolution operator maps an initial quantum state to its state at a later time. For a time-independent Hamiltonian operator H, it is the unitary operator U(t)=e−iHt/ℏ.
Quantum-mechanical propagator (K(qf​,tf​;qi​,ti​))
Words: 96 Articles: 3
Unitary time evolution OurBigBook.com
A quantum-mechanical propagator is the position-space kernel K(qf​,tf​;qi​,ti​)=⟨qf​∣U(tf​,ti​)∣qi​⟩ of the time-evolution operator. It is the amplitude to evolve between the specified endpoint configurations.
Free-particle propagator
Words: 15
Quantum-mechanical propagator OurBigBook.com
For a free particle of mass m on the line,
K(xf​,T;xi​,0)=2πiℏTm​​exp(2ℏTim(xf​−xi​)2​).
(8)
Semiclassical propagator
Words: 57 Articles: 1
Quantum-mechanical propagator OurBigBook.com
A semiclassical propagator sums eiScl​/ℏ over classical paths joining its endpoints, weighted by their quadratic fluctuation determinants and phase indices. It is exact for quadratic actions.
Van Vleck determinant (D)
Words: 30
Semiclassical propagator OurBigBook.com
The Van Vleck determinant is the determinant of mixed endpoint derivatives of a classical action. It measures how nearby classical trajectories focus and supplies the fluctuation prefactor of the semiclassical propagator.
Heisenberg picture
Words: 22
Unitary time evolution OurBigBook.com
In the Heisenberg picture, states are fixed and an observable evolves as
AH​(t)=U(t)†AS​U(t).
(9)
For a time-independent Schrödinger-picture observable,
dtdAH​​=ℏi​[H,AH​].
(10)
Interaction picture
Words: 29
Unitary time evolution OurBigBook.com
For H=H0​+Hint​, the interaction picture moves the free evolution into operators and leaves states to evolve with HI​(t)=eiH0​tHint​e−iH0​t. Its evolution operator is the time-ordered Dyson series.
Time-reversal symmetry in quantum mechanics
Words: 107 Articles: 2
Unitary time evolution OurBigBook.com
A time-reversal operator T intertwines forward and backward evolution:
U(t)T=TU(−t).
(11)
It must be antiunitary in ordinary quantum mechanics. Its conjugate linearity sends i to −i, allowing it to commute with a time-reversal-invariant Hamiltonian rather than reversing the sign of its energy.
Unitary time reversal reverses the energy spectrum
Words: 37
Time-reversal symmetry in quantum mechanics OurBigBook.com
If a unitary T satisfied U(t)T=TU(−t), differentiation at zero would give
HT=−TH.
(12)
It would map every energy E to −E. A Hamiltonian unbounded above would consequently be unbounded below and have no stable ground state.
Antiunitary time reversal preserves the energy spectrum
Words: 28
Time-reversal symmetry in quantum mechanics OurBigBook.com
For antiunitary T, conjugate linearity gives T(iψ)=−iTψ. Differentiating
U(t)T=TU(−t)
(13)
therefore yields HT=TH. Time reversal maps an energy eigenspace to itself and creates no negative-energy instability.

Bound state

Words: 13
Quantum state OurBigBook.com
A bound state is a normalizable energy eigenstate spatially confined by a potential.

Stationary state

Words: 15
Quantum state OurBigBook.com
A stationary state is an energy eigenstate whose time dependence is only an overall phase.

Particle in a ring

Words: 33
Quantum mechanics OurBigBook.com
A quantum particle constrained to a circle has integer angular-momentum eigenvalues and periodic position eigenfunctions. Its propagator can be written either as a sum over angular momenta or as a sum over winding number sectors.

Planck constant (h)

Words: 15
Quantum mechanics OurBigBook.com
The reduced Planck constant is ℏ=h/(2π) and sets the scale of quantum commutators and phases.

Wavefunction

Words: 363 Articles: 17
Quantum mechanics OurBigBook.com
A wavefunction is a complex amplitude whose squared modulus gives a probability density.

Matter wave

Words: 91 Articles: 4
Wavefunction OurBigBook.com
A matter wave is the quantum wave associated with a material particle. Its phase can interfere after coherent paths recombine.

Matter-wave interference

Words: 18
Matter wave OurBigBook.com
Matter-wave interference occurs when coherent spatial branches of a particle's wavefunction recombine and their relative quantum phase changes the detection probabilities.

de Broglie wavelength (λ=h/p)

Words: 14
Matter wave OurBigBook.com
The de Broglie wavelength of a particle with momentum magnitude p is λ=h/p.

Neutron interferometer

Words: 39 Articles: 1
Matter wave OurBigBook.com
A neutron interferometer coherently splits and recombines neutron matter waves, allowing path-dependent phases to be measured through the output intensity.
Colella–Overhauser–Werner experiment
Words: 19
Neutron interferometer OurBigBook.com
The Colella–Overhauser–Werner experiment observed the relative phase acquired by neutron paths at different heights in the Earth's gravitational field.
doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.34.1472

Plane wave

Words: 22
Wavefunction OurBigBook.com
A plane wave has constant amplitude and a phase linear in space and time. It is a momentum eigenstate and is not spatially normalizable.

Probability amplitude

Words: 119 Articles: 4
Wavefunction OurBigBook.com
A probability amplitude is a complex coefficient whose squared modulus gives the probability of the associated measurement outcome.

Born rule

Words: 101 Articles: 3
Probability amplitude OurBigBook.com
The Born rule assigns probability ∣⟨a∣ψ⟩∣2 to outcome a when a normalized state ∣ψ⟩ is measured in an orthonormal eigenbasis.
Wigner theorem
Words: 44 Articles: 1
Born rule OurBigBook.com
Every bijection of pure-state rays that preserves transition probabilities is induced by either a unitary or an antiunitary operator on the Hilbert space.
Projective unitary representation
Words: 21
Wigner theorem OurBigBook.com
Because state vectors differing by a quantum phase represent the same ray, a unitary realization of a group action need only satisfy
U(g1​)U(g2​)=eiϕ(g1​,g2​)U(g1​g2​).
(14)
Energy measurement
Words: 36
Born rule OurBigBook.com
An ideal energy measurement returns an eigenvalue of the Hamiltonian with probability equal to the squared norm of the state's projection onto its eigenspace. After obtaining a nondegenerate energy, the state is the corresponding energy eigenstate.

Normalizable wavefunction

Words: 24
Wavefunction OurBigBook.com
A wavefunction is normalizable when the integral of its squared modulus is finite, so multiplication by a constant can make its total probability one.

Probability density

Words: 13
Wavefunction OurBigBook.com
A probability density is a nonnegative function whose integral over an event gives its probability.

Probability current

Words: 55 Articles: 2
Wavefunction OurBigBook.com
For a nonrelativistic particle of mass m, the probability current is
J=−2miℏ​(ψ∗∇ψ−ψ∇ψ∗).
(15)

Probability continuity equation

Words: 41 Articles: 1
Probability current OurBigBook.com
For a wavefunction satisfying the Schrodinger equation with a real potential,
∂t∂∣ψ∣2​+∇⋅J=0.
(16)
This continuity equation expresses local conservation of probability.
Conservation of quantum probability
Words: 24
Probability continuity equation OurBigBook.com
If the probability current of a normalizable wavefunction vanishes at spatial infinity, integrating the probability continuity equation over all space shows that the total probability ∫∣ψ∣2 is constant in time.

Gaussian wave packet

Words: 28
Wavefunction OurBigBook.com
A Gaussian wave packet is a wavefunction whose spatial amplitude is a Gaussian function. Free quantum evolution preserves its Gaussian form while changing its complex width and spreading its probability density.

Potential barrier

Words: 72 Articles: 2
Quantum mechanics OurBigBook.com
A potential barrier is a region where the potential energy exceeds that in the surrounding regions.

Quantum tunnelling

Words: 56 Articles: 1
Potential barrier OurBigBook.com
Quantum tunnelling is transmission through a potential barrier even when the particle energy is below the barrier height.

Finite square barrier transmission at half barrier height

Words: 40
Quantum tunnelling OurBigBook.com
For a square potential barrier of width 2a and height U0​=2E, put
k=ℏ2mE​​.
(17)
The oscillatory wavenumber outside and decay constant inside are both k. Matching the wavefunction and its derivative at both faces gives transmission amplitude
t=cosh(2ka)e−2ika​
(18)
and transmission probability sech2(2ka).

Hermitian operator on a nonorthogonal two-state basis

Words: 65 Articles: 1
Quantum mechanics OurBigBook.com
For normalized independent states with H∣ψ⟩=g∣ϕ⟩ and H∣ϕ⟩=g∗∣ψ⟩, Hermiticity is equivalent to g⟨ψ∣ϕ⟩∈R. Writing r=g⟨ψ∣ϕ⟩/∣g∣, the orthonormal eigenstates are proportional to
(g∗/∣g∣)∣ψ⟩±∣ϕ⟩
(19)
with eigenvalues ±∣g∣ and squared norms 2(1±r).

Commuting time-dependent two-state Hamiltonian
